module: Safe and healthy diets for all

keywords.name: Food intake
keywords.definition: The act of consuming food.
keywords.short_description: The act of consuming food

keywords.name: Healthy diets
keywords.definition: A healthy diet is a foundation for health, well-being, optimal growth and development. It protects against all forms of malnutrition and includes a diet high in whole grains, vegetables, fruit, legumes and nuts, and low in salt, free sugars and fats, particularly saturated and trans fats.
keywords.short_description: Whole grains, legumes, fruit and vegetables

keywords.name: Nutrient intake throughout life
keywords.definition: Nutrients (carbohydrates, fat, protein, vitamins and minerals) consumed by infants, children, adolescents, adults and older adults.
keywords.short_description: Nutrients eaten by all age groups

keywords.name: Diet-related health conditions
keywords.definition: Physical and mental wellbeing negatively impacted by dietary intake.
keywords.short_description: Negative impacts of unhealthful diets

keywords.name: Diet-related chronic disease
keywords.definition: Long-lasting health conditions that are significantly influenced by dietary factors. For example, obesity, cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes and certain types of cancer.
keywords.short_description: E.g., obesity, type 2 diabetes

keywords.name: Population weight status
keywords.definition: Usually assessed using Body Mass Index (BMI) and can be categorised into underweight, normal weight, overweight or obese.
keywords.short_description: BMI assessment

keywords.name: Food safety and risk mitigation
keywords.definition: Identifying potential safety hazards in the production, cooking or storage of food and implementing measures to reduce or eliminate these hazards.
keywords.short_description: Avoiding hazards in preparation or storage

keywords.name: Foodborne microbiological, physical and chemical contaminants
keywords.definition: Foodborne illnesses are usually infectious or toxic in nature and caused by bacteria, viruses, parasites or chemical substances entering the body through contaminated food.
keywords.short_description: E.g., food poisoning or disease

keywords.name: Food integrity
keywords.definition: A multidimensional concept concerning the integrity of product, process, people and data, implying that a food product is intact, safe, of quality and authentic, as well as ethically sourced and distributed.
keywords.short_description: Honesty in claims and production methods

keywords.name: Environmental sustainability claims
keywords.definition: Sustainability claims must adhere to the Green Claims Code, ensuring claims made are substantiated, truthful and accurate.
keywords.short_description: Truthful environmental sustainability claims

keywords.name: Food fraud
keywords.definition: The deliberate and intentional substitution, addition, tampering, or misrepresentation of food, food ingredients, or packaging for economic gain.
keywords.short_description: Unlawful actions to deceive end-consumer

keywords.name: Nutrition and health claims
keywords.definition: Nutritional claims relate to energy, fat, sugar, fibre, protein, salt and vitamins and minerals. Health claims imply a benefit to health, e.g., vitamin C contributes to immune function.
keywords.short_description: E.g., nutritionally fat-free or benefiting health

keywords.name: Transparency of production of products deriving from animals
keywords.definition: Clear, transparent labelling and traceability where products derived from animals were produced and the methods used.
keywords.short_description: Information about where and how the food was made

module: Economically thriving, robust food value chains

keywords.name: Innovative and transformative businesses
keywords.definition: Organisations that introduce new products or make changes to their processes, technologies, culture and strategy.
keywords.short_description: New solutions and modern processes

keywords.name: Agrifood investment
keywords.definition: The allocation of capital to support food system core activities, such as production, processing, retailing and managing waste.
keywords.short_description: Money provided for core food system activities

keywords.name: Knowledge and skills
keywords.definition: Knowledge refers to factual information; skills are the practical abilities to apply that knowledge to certain situations.
keywords.short_description: Remembering facts and having applicable skills

keywords.name: Business practices and technology
keywords.definition: Business practices involve increased digitisation and data-driven decision making; technologies include robotics, big data, AI and genetic editing.
keywords.short_description: E.g., digitisation, AI and data analytics

keywords.name: Economic development
keywords.definition: The process of improving the economic, political, and social well-being of people by increasing quality of life.
keywords.short_description: Improving living standards

keywords.name: Investment attractiveness
keywords.definition: How appealing a company, industry or location is for investment, based on profitability and risk assessment.
keywords.short_description: Involves assessment of risk and potential profitability

keywords.name: Profit
keywords.definition: Total revenue minus total cost.
keywords.short_description: Total revenue minus total cost

keywords.name: Revenue
keywords.definition: Total income generated by the sale of goods and services.
keywords.short_description: Total income generated by the sale of goods and services

keywords.name: Yield
keywords.definition: In economics, the percentage return on investments; in agriculture, the amount of crop produced per land area.
keywords.short_description: Return on investment or crops produced per area

keywords.name: Value chain configuration
keywords.definition: How people and their activities along the value chain interact.
keywords.short_description: Core food system activity interactions

keywords.name: Commercial risk management
keywords.definition: The systematic process of identifying, assessing, and mitigating threats that can affect an organisation’s success.
keywords.short_description: Identifying and assessing risks

keywords.name: Consumer habits
keywords.definition: Mental and physical activities consumers engage in when evaluating, purchasing and using products.
keywords.short_description: People’s shopping and usage habits

keywords.name: Degree of structural reconfiguration
keywords.definition: The degree to which proportions and relations between food system activities and workforces change.
keywords.short_description: Core food system activity changes

keywords.name: Food loss
keywords.definition: Food loss takes place on the farm and through supply chains due to sub-optimal farming, poor storage or inflexible distribution.
keywords.short_description: Foods lost throughout the supply chain

keywords.name: Packaging
keywords.definition: Materials used to wrap or protect goods, from sacks to crisp packets.
keywords.short_description: Protecting foods

keywords.name: Responsible sourcing
keywords.definition: Procurement that is sustainable and ethical, respecting human rights.
keywords.short_description: Sustainable, ethical procurement

keywords.name: Competitive positioning
keywords.definition: Competition in the food system for efficiency and output, affecting prices and environmental impacts.
keywords.short_description: Efficient systems and increased output

keywords.name: Food self-sufficiency
keywords.definition: The ratio of domestic production to consumption; lack of self-sufficiency increases market vulnerability.
keywords.short_description: Food produced to meet own requirements

keywords.name: Trading relationships
keywords.definition: Economic exchanges between countries, determined by tariffs and trade policies.
keywords.short_description: Trade between countries

keywords.name: Atmosphere
keywords.definition: A layer of gas and suspended solids surrounding Earth’s surface.
keywords.short_description: Gas surrounding the Earth

keywords.name: Air quality
keywords.definition: Describes how polluted the air we breathe is; poor air quality can be hazardous to health.
keywords.short_description: Levels of pollution in the air

keywords.name: Greenhouse gas emissions
keywords.definition: Gases like CO2, CH4, N2O, and water vapour that trap heat and regulate Earth’s temperature.
keywords.short_description: E.g., carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide and water vapour

keywords.name: Water vapour
keywords.definition: The most abundant greenhouse gas; increases with warming and can affect crops and pathogens.
keywords.short_description: Humidity is caused by water vapour

keywords.name: Biosphere
keywords.definition: Areas occupied by living organisms, including oceans, forests, and land.
keywords.short_description: Areas occupied by living organisms

keywords.name: Biomass
keywords.definition: Organic, non-fossil material of biological origin (plants and animals).
keywords.short_description: Quantity of living organisms (plants and animals)

keywords.name: Functional biodiversity
keywords.definition: Variety of biological and chemical roles organisms perform in an ecosystem.
keywords.short_description: Variety of roles or functions within an ecosystem

keywords.name: Genetic diversity
keywords.definition: Within one species, the range of genetic characteristics.
keywords.short_description: Within one species, the range of genetic characteristics

keywords.name: Net primary productivity
keywords.definition: Net flux of carbon from the atmosphere into green plants per unit time.
keywords.short_description: Net flux of carbon from the atmosphere into green plants

keywords.name: Species richness
keywords.definition: The number of different species present in an ecosystem.
keywords.short_description: Quantity of different species

keywords.name: Geosphere
keywords.definition: Earth’s interior and surface, comprising all rocks.
keywords.short_description: Internal and surface rocks forming the Earth

keywords.name: Non-renewable resources
keywords.definition: Energy resources like coal, gas, oil, and nuclear energy that cannot be replaced once used.
keywords.short_description: Once used, cannot be replaced

keywords.name: Soil carbon
keywords.definition: Organic carbon in soil, an indicator of soil health and biological activity.
keywords.short_description: Organic carbon found in soil

keywords.name: Soil degradation
keywords.definition: Change in soil health resulting in reduced ecosystem capacity.
keywords.short_description: Reduction in soil health

keywords.name: Soil erosion and deposition
keywords.definition: Loss of topsoil and nutrients, worsened by poor management.
keywords.short_description: Soil losses

keywords.name: Hydrosphere
keywords.definition: All water on Earth: surface, underground, and atmospheric.
keywords.short_description: All water on Earth

keywords.name: Freshwater extraction
keywords.definition: Taking water from lakes, rivers, or groundwater for human or industrial use.
keywords.short_description: Removing water from lakes, rivers or groundwater

keywords.name: Nitrogen and phosphorous loading
keywords.definition: Increased input of nutrients into the environment, affecting ecosystems and water quality.
keywords.short_description: Increasing input of nutrients into environment

keywords.name: Water quality
keywords.definition: Chemical, physical, and biological characteristics determining water purity.
keywords.short_description: E.g., chemicals, physical characteristics, biological

keywords.name: Water temperature
keywords.definition: How hot or cold water is, measured in °C.
keywords.short_description: Hot or cold

module: Just, ethical, fair and culturally meaningful food system

keywords.name: Right to food
keywords.definition: Food security exists when all people have physical and economic access to sufficient, safe and nutritious food at all times.
keywords.short_description: Access to sufficient, safe and nutritious food

keywords.name: Access
keywords.definition: The ability to equitably access food physically, economically and socially.
keywords.short_description: Everyone should be able to access food

keywords.name: Agency
keywords.definition: The capacity to make decisions regarding one's own body and personal wellbeing.
keywords.short_description: Decision-making autonomy

keywords.name: Cultural appropriateness
keywords.definition: Degree to which accessible food satisfies cultural norms.
keywords.short_description: Degree to which accessible food satisfies cultural norms

keywords.name: Food culture
keywords.definition: The wider set of beliefs, values, and factors that influence what, when, why and how individuals eat.
keywords.short_description: Beliefs and values around food

keywords.name: Food behaviour
keywords.definition: Habits and actions related to selecting, preparing, consuming and disposing food.
keywords.short_description: Habits around food selection, preparation, consumption and disposal

keywords.name: Food environment
keywords.definition: External and personal factors that shape people’s food acquisition and consumption.
keywords.short_description: External and personal factors create the food environment

keywords.name: Food literacy
keywords.definition: Proficiency in food-related skills and knowledge.
keywords.short_description: Food related skills and knowledge

keywords.name: Food waste
keywords.definition: Food wasted at the consumer level, either at home or outside.
keywords.short_description: Food wasted at the consumer level

keywords.name: Social justice
keywords.definition: Aims to give individuals and groups fair treatment and equal share of social, environmental and economic benefits.
keywords.short_description: Give everyone fair treatment and equality

keywords.name: Dignified work environments
keywords.definition: Encompasses humane work conditions, diversity, and opportunities for meaningful contribution.
keywords.short_description: Decent work conditions and meaningfulness

keywords.name: Social externalities
keywords.definition: Hidden social costs occurring during food system activities, such as underpayment or forced labour.
keywords.short_description: ‘Hidden’ social costs across the food system

keywords.name: Environmental justice
keywords.definition: Distribution of environmental benefits and burdens experienced by groups of people.
keywords.short_description: Environmental benefits and burdens

keywords.name: Environmental externalities
keywords.definition: Hidden environmental costs during food system activities, such as pollution or soil depletion.
keywords.short_description: ‘Hidden’ environmental costs occurring across the food system

keywords.name: Recognition of nature’s contribution to human wellbeing
keywords.definition: Ecosystem services like pollination, carbon sequestration, and water filtration that benefit humans.
keywords.short_description: E.g., climate regulation, food, stress relief

keywords.name: Animal welfare
keywords.definition: Owners and keepers must ensure animals’ needs are met for environment, diet, behaviour and protection from harm.
keywords.short_description: The physical and mental state of animals

keywords.name: Treatment during production, transport and slaughter
keywords.definition: Five domains to consider for animal welfare: nutrition, environment, health, behaviour, and mental state.
keywords.short_description: Consideration of animals’ physical and psychological wellbeing
